final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and expressly conceded the key evidentiary gaps. The response is mainly a reframing of the same record: aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and reversible rollout controls are supported, but the same admissible evidence also shows a material weakness in the mortgage servicing assistant segment, continued exposure of that segment in rollout, an unsigned risk-acceptance draft that does not address that exposure, and a policy requiring disclosure unless the limitation is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. That matters for proportionality: a narrowed, caveated position can justify compliant_with_caveats only when the caveat is actually satisfied or independently evidenced. Here, the proposed caveat depends on actual pre-launch disclosure, but the record still does not show that disclosure occurred. So the caveat is not just narrowing language; it remains an unresolved compliance predicate. On this record, the packet is plausibly a qualified warning about certification risk, but it is still not supported as a compliant certification basis.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the final pre-launch model card or launch artifact actually disclosed the mortgage servicing assistant limitation.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance for the exposed mortgage servicing assistant segment.
The affected mortgage servicing assistant segment remains eligible in the initial rollout cohort.
Policy text says rollout controls and post-launch monitoring do not satisfy the predicate when the affected segment remains exposed without exclusion or reviewed risk acceptance.
The Actor's narrowed framing is more defensible as a description of an unresolved gap than as evidence that certification is compliant, even with caveats.
